title: 2005 AMC 10A Problem 11
statement: A wooden cube \(n\) units on a side is painted red on all six faces and then cut into \(n^3\) unit cubes. Exactly one-fourth of the total number of faces of the unit cubes are red. What is \(n?\)

solutions.text:
The unit cubes have \(6n^3\) faces total, of which the original surface accounts for \(6n^2\) red faces. Then \(\dfrac{6n^2}{6n^3} = \dfrac{1}{n} = \dfrac{1}{4},\) so \(n = 4.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Each of the \(n^3\) unit cubes has \(6\) faces, so there are \(6n^3\) faces in all
Only the original surface is red, contributing \(6n^2\) red faces; set \(\dfrac{6n^2}{6n^3} = \dfrac{1}{4}\)
